correctness.rationale: Saliola’s proven free-band path-algebra isomorphism yields 194 arrows and 100 length-two paths. Each of the 20 intermediate subsets of size two or three has exactly five entering and one leaving arrow, or the reverse; the 120 involved arrows and their 100 paths form 20 mutually orthogonal 11-dimensional nilpotent radical blocks, with 74 remaining annihilator arrows. Opposite blocks give isomorphic algebra groups by polynomial inversion, over every field. A direct bilinear commutator-rank trichotomy (0,1,5) gives the conjugacy-class-size polynomial, and the scalar coordinate zero/nonzero partition gives the all-arity formula. The finite checker exhaustively confirms indicated instances; finite checks are corroboration rather than a proof of unbounded claims.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The two-tuple total and the underlying radical decomposition are not independently new in view of these results; they are marked as antecedents. The theorem here makes the five-letter quiver-specific 20-block inventory explicit and computes individual conjugacy class sizes with their distribution, plus all tuple lengths. A known broad algebra-isomorphism tool alone does not enumerate those finer invariants without the additional orbit-rank and tuple-classification calculations. There remains a real possibility that these are recorded as corollaries elsewhere.

The prior pair count determines only the total class number, not the sizes of the separate classes, and the cited invariant-ring results do not address the group. The direct block and commutator-rank proof establishes this additional information. One cannot rule out other stronger literature, as recorded in residual risks.

originality.rationale: The strongest compared paper, Hennecart–Perry 2022, gives radical-preserving splitting and counts commuting pairs for short quivers; this covers the s=2 total and supplies an implicit decomposition method. The present distinct claim concerns the complete 20-factor conjugacy-class-size distribution, including forbidden exponents, and arbitrary-arity commuting counts for the specific five-generator free-band radical. Neither that paper, Saliola’s source path-algebra work, nor the invariant-ring study states these fine distributions. Residual risk of prior consequences or hidden equivalences is recorded explicitly; search absence is not regarded as proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: Hennecart–Perry’s broad radical-preserving operations and short-quiver pair formulas are powerful enough that the specific group factorization and two-tuple specialization should be regarded as previously implied. The status of the finer class-size and higher-arity formulas as unrecorded consequences cannot be exhaustively established.
A stronger unlocated classification of conjugacy strata in free-band radical units or of arbitrary commuting tuples in rectangular unipotent groups might imply the theorem.

value.rationale: A natural complete class-size distribution and all-arity commuting profile are determined for the principal unipotent group of an explicitly defined 326-dimensional semigroup algebra. The 294-dimensional radical has twenty nonabelian blocks and the resulting conjugacy-class spectrum has exactly six missing exponents below the maximal size. The rank-five case is the largest free-band rank with radical cube zero (at six generators length-three paths appear), making it a meaningful arithmetic threshold and a refinement of the studied Higman-type pair counts rather than an arbitrary parameter census.
